About the Company 

 Redesign Health 
 
 is a global venture and applied technology firm focused on building next-generation healthcare companies. We manage venture capital and venture buyout strategies, each powered by an AI operating system and team of leading technologists, entrepreneurs, and investors.

 Our venture capital strategy backs exceptional founders at the earliest stage, often before an idea is fully formed, often providing the first institutional capital and an unmatched degree of strategic healthcare-specific leverage through exit. Our venture buyout strategy partners with proven management teams at existing incumbents via control investments and delivers outsized value by rewiring core products and workflows with AI.

 Since inception in 2018, Redesign and our portfolio companies have touched the lives of more than 15 million patients, raised over $1.5 billion from premier institutional, sovereign, and strategic investors, and built distinctive partnerships with marquee healthcare organizations around the world.

 Redesign is based in New York and has offices in Bengaluru, Los Angeles, and Riyadh.

 About the Cedars-Sinai / Redesign Health Partnership 

 Redesign Health and Cedars-Sinai have launched a Digital Innovation Platform, a first-of-its-kind venture creation engine embedded inside one of the world’s premier academic medical centers. The platform combines Redesign’s healthcare company-building methodology with something no standalone venture firm can offer: Cedars-Sinai’s 4,500+ physicians and nurses, its expansive clinical network of 40+ hospitals and sites of care, a purpose-built synthetic and de-identified data platform, and a standing commitment to serve as the first customer for every company the platform creates. Ideas originate from the clinicians and researchers who see problems up close every day. The companies that emerge are validated in real clinical environments before they ever reach the broader market.

 This is an unparalleled opportunity to build generational healthcare companies. You will have something almost no one in a healthcare venture has: a fully committed institutional partner with world-class clinical expertise, deep data assets, and the infrastructure to pilot and validate at scale - all before a company writes its first check to a customer. The access is real. The commitment is structural, not performative.

 For the full list of exclusive benefits as part of the Redesign Health and Cedars-Sinai partnership, explore the article 
 
 here .

 About the Role 

 Most healthcare investors wait for companies to come to them. This role creates them.

 As a New Ventures Associate, you will research opportunities across the healthcare landscape to identify space for new venture backable companies to be built or scale. You will build the competitive landscapes and market analyses that separate real opportunities from noise, and help turn that work into investment theses the team can act on. Our job is to evaluate and identify the right opportunities for venture creation and/or scaling while directing other solutions to the proper channel within the Cedars-Sinai organization. You will continue to develop the infrastructure that lets us do this repeatedly and you will spend real time in the local innovation community, building the relationships with investors and founders.

 This is a strong role for someone early in their career who wants to get exposure to venture at the heart of where healthcare is delivered through a truly unique partnership. You will work directly with New Ventures and Cedars-Sinai leadership, help turn thematic research into opportunities to fund companies, and have access to clinical and institutional partners.

 We are looking for someone with 1 to 3 years of experience in investing (banking, venture, PE, or other relevant areas) or research (consulting, strategy, other relevant areas) including with a preference for candidates with exposure to healthcare and digital health. We’r looking for someone with sharp analytical judgment, genuine curiosity about healthcare innovation, and the ability to earn credibility with clinicians, operators, and entrepreneurs. You should be able to move quickly, be comfortable with ambiguity, and provide succinct answers to complex problems.

 This position is based in Los Angeles and will work onsite 3-4 days per week in our Cedars-Sinai office.

 What You’ll Do: 

• Evaluate and research commercial opportunities in healthcare.

• Identify Commercially Viable Opportunities: Find opportunities that address specific challenges within Cedars-Sinai and are emblematic of systemic challenges that health systems across the country face, ensuring they are strategically aligned with organizational goals.

• Redesign Research: Apply Redesign Health’s scoring frameworks and leverage RH venture-building methodologies to evaluate, prioritize, and refine innovation opportunities

• Direct opportunities that don’t meet the level of a new or scalable venture opportunity to the right teams and/or channels that are more appropriate to address those pain points

• Support the Infrastructure for the Digital Innovation Program at Cedars-Sinai

• Socialize the Innovation Program: Foster a culture of creativity and innovation among staff by promoting the innovation program across the organization.

• Meet with Stakeholders: Engage with stakeholders to learn about the various departments and institutes at CS, fostering collaboration and understanding of organizational needs.

• Finalize Opportunity Zones: Driving identification and evaluation of opportunity zones to determine whether we believe there are viable investment theses for company creation.

• Create the End to End Pipes: Leverage the existing infrastructure (i.e., internal submissions, areas of research, founder referrals) to fine tune an end to end pathway of evaluation to execution where every stakeholder feels included in the process.

• Source and Co-ideate with founders once an opportunity is identified

• Build and maintain a strong network of external founders, continuously cultivating relationships with entrepreneurs aligned with Cedars-Sinai's strategic priorities.

• Evaluate external founders for partnership and company creation opportunities that advance Cedars-Sinai's mission and innovation objectives.

• Serve as a thought partner throughout venture development, providing strategic guidance before and after operating company (OpCo) formation.

• Facilitate meaningful connections between founders and Cedars-Sinai stakeholders, resources, clinicians, and ecosystem partners.

• Lead the development and launch of new venture-backed companies that leverage validated opportunities and create meaningful impact across the healthcare ecosystem.

• Successfully launch at least one new company annually in partnership with a founder, translating identified opportunities into scalable healthcare businesses.

 What You’ll Need 

• 1–3+ years of experience in venture capital, early-stage investing, startups, or a related field

• Healthcare domain expertise preferred with the ability to develop original investment theses across care delivery, health tech, and digital health

• Fluency in business model analysis, primary and secondary research, investment thesis development, and financial modeling

• Bachelor’s degree required with demonstrated academic excellence

 Core Competencies

• 
 Institutional Credibility: You hold your own in a room with senior clinicians and health system executives. You have worked inside or alongside a complex organization and understand how decisions actually get made, who needs to be brought along, and how to be useful to the people building internal support.

• 
 Analytical Rigor: 
 
 You take an ambiguous question about a market and turn it into a clear, defensible answer. You build competitive landscapes, size markets, and pressure-test your own assumptions, and you can tell the difference between a finding that holds up and one that just looks clean. You know when an analysis is solid enough to act on and when it needs another pass.

• 
 Commercial Curiosity: 
 
 You want to understand how businesses actually make money. You think about who pays, why they pay, and whether a model can hold up, and your questions get sharper as your sense for healthcare economics develops. You are not expected to have the final read yet, but you are building toward it.

• 
 Bias to Output: 
 
 You move work forward without being managed through it. You hold several threads at once, hit your commitments, and produce clean material the team can put in front of leadership. When something is stuck, you surface it early rather than letting it drift.

 Behavioral Skills

• 
 Self-Starter: 
 
 You are comfortable working independently and can own the execution of your own responsibilities. You are proactive in transforming your workflows and don’t wait for someone else to tell you something is wrong or should be improved.

• 
 Clear Communicator: Able to translate analyses into concise insights for senior leaders, investment committees, and management teams.

• 
 Entrepreneurial: 
 
 You are resourceful, proactive, and comfortable building from ambiguity. You treat the sourcing engine itself as a product to be developed.

• 
 Bias for Action: Thrives in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment characterized by urgency, ownership, and adaptability.

• 
 Technology Innovator: You proactively leverage AI and emerging technology tools to create extraordinary productivity and impact. You think ahead about how your role will evolve and independently experiment with, adopt, and refine technology-driven solutions.

About General Atlantic 

 General Atlantic is a leading global investor with more than four and a half decades of experience providing capital and strategic support for over 885 companies throughout its history. Established in 1980, General Atlantic continues to be a dedicated partner to visionary founders and investors seeking to build dynamic businesses and create lasting value. Guided by the conviction that entrepreneurs can be incredible agents of transformational change, the firm combines a collaborative global approach, sector specific expertise, a long-term investment horizon, and a deep understanding of growth drivers to partner with and scale innovative businesses around the world. The firm leverages its patient capital, operational expertise, and global platform to support a diversified investment platform spanning Growth Equity, Infrastructure, and Strategic Solutions. General Atlantic manages approximately $126 billion in assets under management, inclusive of all strategies, as of March 31, 2026, with more than 900 professionals in 20 countries across five regions. For more information on General Atlantic, please visit www.generalatlantic.com. 

 General Atlantic Life Sciences Practice 

 The GA Life Sciences practice provides capital and strategic support for development stage biopharma companies, with an established track record across public and private investments. The Life Sciences team focuses on novel therapies that provide substantial patient benefit and have the potential to redefine standards of care. GA’s differentiated approach to life sciences is characterized by highly thematic investing, scaling significant capital into companies as they advance through clinical development and commercialization, and partnering with management teams to generate value. Investments include Akero Therapeutics (acquired by Novo Nordisk), Karuna Therapeutics (acquired by BMS), Cincor Pharma (acquired by AstraZeneca), and Centessa Pharmaceuticals (potential acquisition by Eli Lilly).

 Position Summary 

 General Atlantic is seeking a Life Sciences investor to join our New York‑based investment team. This role will have exposure to all parts of the investment process, including evaluating new investment opportunities and investment themes in biopharma and life science companies, conducting technical diligence, supporting deal execution, and working with portfolio companies. The ideal candidate will have a scientific background (MD or PhD) and at least two years of relevant industry experience, with the goal of driving strategic growth and generating value for the firm’s portfolio.

 Responsibilities 

• Source, evaluate, and recommend investment opportunities in drug development / biopharmaceutical companies including development and ownership of thematic focus areas

• Support scientific and clinical due diligence, integrating preclinical data, clinical trial results, regulatory strategy, and market dynamics into investment recommendations

• Develop and present rigorous investment theses to senior stakeholders, including the global Investment Committee

• Contribute across the full deal process, including coordination of third-party scientific advisors, KOLs, and commercial consultants

• Monitor portfolio companies and support the GA team’s efforts in capital allocation and value creation

• Leverage clinical and industry networks to generate proprietary deal flow and market intelligence

• Collaborate with professionals across the firm and foster exceptional knowledge-sharing

 Qualifications 

• MD or PhD in relevant scientific field (molecular biology, genetics, biology, chemistry, etc.)

• 2-5 years of post-graduate school professional experience, including at least 2 years of relevant experience in the life sciences sector (e.g., life sciences investing, life sciences strategy consulting, life sciences equity research / investment banking, biopharma operating role)

• Ability to analyze and integrate data from various sources into investment recommendations, including preclinical and clinical data, FDA/regulatory correspondence, and market research

• Strong foundation in financial modeling with a demonstrated commitment to deepening analytical expertise

• Passion for primary scientific literature, including scientific/medical meetings and conferences

• High degree of familiarity with drug development and regulatory processes

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to synthesize and present complex information clearly

• Demonstrated maturity and professional presence; comfortable interacting with senior executives and management teams

• Highly motivated, inquisitive, and a positive, can-do attitude

• Ability to take ownership, work independently, manage multiple priorities, and thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment

 GA Value 

 General Atlantic offers a robust reward program to all employees that will support you and your family, maintaining fulfilling, secure and healthy lives now and into the future, which includes but is not limited to medical insurance, retirement savings contributions, mental and physical health resources and an equal pay program that allows you to earn a base salary of $150,000 –160,000   of which the exact amount offered will be driven by the degree to which you meet role requirements, additional special skills and experience.  Additional reward programs, such as annual discretionary bonuses and long-term incentive programs, are available for eligible employees and are offered as recognition for performance and one’s contributions towards the organization’s success.
